hints.title: Pyramid Overflow Cascading Obstacle
hints.text: Poured liquid fills glass (r, c) up to 1 cup, and any excess splits evenly into glasses (r + 1, c) and (r + 1, c + 1). How can cascading overflow row by row determine how full a specific glass becomes?

hints.title: Bifurcated Spillover Invariant
hints.text: If glass (r, c) receives V cups with V > 1, exactly (V - 1) / 2 cups spill into glass (r + 1, c) and (V - 1) / 2 cups into glass (r + 1, c + 1).

hints.title: Row-by-Row Flow Simulation Procedure
hints.text: Initialize a row array with the single element poured. For each row from 0 up to query_row - 1, allocate the next row of size row + 2. For each glass c, if liquid exceeds 1.0, add half the excess to next row glasses c and c + 1. Return min(1.0, query row glass value).

hints.title: Complete Implementation

complexity.notes: Simulates liquid flow row by row up to query_row with R * (R + 1) / 2 glass updates.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Tracing individual droplets across exponential geometric splits is intractable.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Storing only the current row of glasses consumes O(R) memory.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Capping the final answer at 1.0 while letting intermediate overflow cascade without early truncation.
